name: Dynamic NPC Interaction Prioritization
consequences: Focusing on real-time decision-driven NPC behavior increases immersion but demands advanced AI systems that may delay development. A scripted approach ensures predictability but risks player disengagement through repetitive interactions.
options: Implement AI-driven NPC relationships with evolving player influence
Design scripted NPC interactions with branching dialogue trees
Create a hybrid system with limited AI-driven responses in key story moments
review: AI-driven interactions require significant technical investment, risking delays, while scripted systems may feel artificial despite lower development costs.

name: Procedural Generation Trade-offs
consequences: Maximizing procedural content reduces manual design work but may create repetitive environments. Focusing on handcrafted zones ensures quality but limits world size and exploration variety.
options: Generate terrain and architecture procedurally with manual tuning
Build core zones manually while using procedural systems for peripheral areas
Develop a modular procedural framework for dynamic event placement
review: Procedural systems risk homogenization without careful calibration, while manual design constraints may hinder scalability.

name: Multiplayer Integration Model
consequences: Embedding persistent multiplayer elements enhances long-term engagement but complicates single-player narrative cohesion. A standalone multiplayer mode preserves focus but reduces cross-platform synergy.
options: Create a shared world with synchronized player-driven events
Develop separate single-player and multiplayer campaigns with thematic ties
Implement asynchronous multiplayer mechanics within the single-player experience
review: Persistent multiplayer systems introduce technical complexity that may compromise single-player polish without careful resource allocation.

name: Criminal Economy Complexity
consequences: A fully dynamic economy with player-driven markets increases realism but requires extensive balancing. A simplified system with predefined tiers ensures stability but limits emergent gameplay.
options: Design a market-driven economy with player-speculative trading mechanics
Implement a structured economy with fixed resource hierarchies
Create a hybrid system with key dynamic elements and static core mechanics
review: Dynamic economies demand ongoing maintenance and risk imbalance, while static systems may feel restrictive despite lower development risk.

name: Vehicle Customization Scope
consequences: Extensive customization options boost player investment but increase development and testing demands. Limited options streamline production but may frustrate enthusiasts.
options: Offer comprehensive vehicle modding with physics-based customization
Provide a curated selection of high-fidelity, pre-designed vehicles
Implement a balanced system with core customization and restricted modding
review: Comprehensive modding capabilities require ongoing support and may introduce technical issues, while limited options risk player dissatisfaction.

name: Urban Layering Strategy
consequences: Prioritizing historical architectural accuracy in city zones accelerates asset creation but limits narrative flexibility for fictionalized crime scenarios. Conversely, abstracted urban layouts reduce development time but risk player disengagement from environmental storytelling.
options: Marry period-specific building silhouettes with fictionalized street layouts
Use procedural texture blending to mix real-world material samples with stylized geometry
Implement dynamic zoning that shifts between realistic and exaggerated urban forms based on player activity
review: Historical accuracy reduces rework in asset pipelines but creates rigid constraints for narrative-driven location changes mid-development.

name: Moral Consequence Weighting
consequences: Immediate karma penalties for unethical actions increase player accountability but force designers to pre-script all possible moral dilemmas. Delayed consequence systems allow greater emergent storytelling but risk player perception of arbitrary punishment.
options: Tie reputation metrics to both public perception and hidden factional influence scores
Create cascading ethical repercussions through interconnected character relationships
Implement randomized moral ambiguity in mission outcomes based on player decision timing
review: Delayed consequence systems require extensive testing to prevent player frustration from perceived unfairness in ethical outcomes.

name: Heist Scalability Framework
consequences: Modular heist design enables content reuse across missions but reduces the uniqueness of high-stakes operations. Customized heist architectures increase development complexity but enhance player memorability of key sequences.
options: Design base mechanics that adapt to different urban infrastructure types
Introduce variable difficulty scaling through real-time AI opponent adjustments
Create hybrid heist modes that blend stealth, combat, and puzzle-solving elements
review: Modular systems risk homogenizing mission design unless paired with strict narrative differentiation between heist types.

name: Asset Optimization Pipeline
consequences: Aggressive texture compression improves performance on lower-end hardware but degrades visual fidelity in key cinematic sequences. High-fidelity assets increase storage requirements and loading times across all platforms.
options: Implement dynamic resolution scaling based on player movement velocity
Create procedural material generation for repetitive environmental elements
Develop adaptive streaming that prioritizes detail based on player attention metrics
review: Visual fidelity trade-offs require continuous player feedback loops to maintain acceptable perception thresholds across hardware variations.

name: Community Feedback Loop Integration
consequences: Early access beta programs generate valuable data but risk leaking unpolished mechanics that shape public expectations. Closed alpha testing preserves design integrity but limits the volume of actionable feedback.
options: Establish tiered feedback channels with different player cohorts for specific design aspects
Create interactive telemetry dashboards for real-time player behavior analysis
Implement seasonal content drops based on aggregated player performance metrics
review: Beta testing introduces alignment risks between developer vision and player-driven feature expectations.

name: Urban Infrastructure Integration
consequences: Prioritizing realistic city layouts enhances immersion but increases development time and resource allocation. Downstream, this risks delaying other features like multiplayer systems or narrative content.
options: Integrate real-world city layouts with fictional elements
Use modular building systems for scalability
Prioritize fictionalized zones for narrative cohesion
review: Balancing authenticity with resource constraints risks delaying other critical features.

name: Criminal Economy Simulation Depth
consequences: Deepening the economy adds realism but complicates player progression. Downstream, it may introduce unintended game balance issues or require extensive testing.
options: Implement dynamic black-market pricing models
Create player-driven illegal enterprises
Simulate regional economic disparities
review: Enhanced realism may introduce complexity that challenges player engagement and game balance.

name: Vehicle Customization Variety
consequences: Expanding customization options increases player satisfaction but demands more development resources. Downstream, it risks performance issues or technical debt.
options: Introduce modifiable vehicle physics parameters
Allow cosmetic and functional upgrades
Enable community-driven vehicle design submissions
review: Higher player engagement risks technical challenges and resource allocation conflicts.

name: Heist Mechanics Complexity
consequences: Adding complex heist mechanics improves replayability but may frustrate casual players. Downstream, it narrows the target audience and increases testing demands.
options: Design multi-layered heist objectives with interdependent tasks
Integrate real-time player collaboration systems
Implement adaptive difficulty based on player skill
review: Enhanced depth may alienate casual players, reducing overall market reach.

name: Moral Consequence Realism
consequences: Realistic moral consequences deepen narrative impact but limit player freedom. Downstream, it could lead to player dissatisfaction or reduced replayability.
options: Create branching narrative outcomes based on choices
Implement systemic societal reactions to player actions
Design irreversible player decisions with long-term impacts
review: Ethical storytelling may conflict with player agency, affecting game appeal.

name: Procedural Generation Diversity
consequences: Diversifying procedural generation enhances world variety but reduces consistency. Downstream, it risks unpredictable player experiences or narrative fragmentation.
options: Use hybrid procedural and handcrafted environments
Generate dynamic event chains tied to player behavior
Adapt terrain features based on player actions
review: Increased variety may compromise world coherence, affecting player immersion.

name: Funding Diversification Approach
consequences: Diversifying funding sources reduces financial risk but complicates stakeholder management. Downstream, it may create conflicting priorities or alignment challenges.
options: Secure industry partnerships with exclusive content access
Apply for government innovation grants with specific deliverables
Establish community-funded development tiers with tiered rewards
review: Multiple funding streams may create alignment challenges, risking project coherence.
